event.title: Egyptian Journalist Lina Attalah Detained Following Court Ruling
event.canonical_title: Egyptian Journalist Lina Attalah Detained Following Court Ruling
event.summary: Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the independent news outlet Mada Masr, was detained by Egyptian security forces after a court ruling that imposed a fine on her. The ruling also ordered the closure of Mada Masr, which has drawn criticism from organizations like Amnesty International, highlighting concerns over press freedom in the country.

timeline.title: Novaya Gazeta, Last Independent Newspaper in Russia, Announces Closure Amid Kremlin Pressure
timeline.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of the last independent newspapers in Russia, has announced its closure due to increasing pressure from the Kremlin. The newspaper has been a vocal critic of the Russian government's actions, particularly regarding the war in Ukraine. This closure marks a significant step in the ongoing crackdown on dissenting voices in Russia.
key_facts: Novaya Gazeta was one of the few independent outlets critical of the Russian government.
The closure is attributed to pressure from state authorities.
The newspaper has been operational for nearly three decades.

event_overview.title: About Press Freedom
event_overview.subject: Press Freedom
event_overview.summary: Press freedom is the ability of journalists and news organizations to gather, publish and distribute information independently, without censorship or improper interference. It is generally treated as part of the broader human right to freedom of expression, while international standards allow only restrictions that are established by law and necessary for specified legitimate aims.

facts.label: Meaning
facts.value: UNESCO describes press freedom as the right of journalists and press organizations to operate independently without censorship or interference by public authorities or other entities.

facts.label: International legal basis
facts.value: Article 19 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights protects the freedom to seek, receive and impart information and ideas across frontiers through any media; it permits restrictions only when provided by law and necessary for the listed purposes.

facts.label: Media independence
facts.value: UN human-rights guidance says freedom of expression includes the ability of a free, independent and diverse press and media to comment on public issues without censorship or restraint, alongside the public's interest in receiving information.

facts.label: International observance
facts.value: World Press Freedom Day is observed annually on 3 May. The UN General Assembly proclaimed it in 1993 following a 1991 UNESCO General Conference recommendation; it is intended to affirm press-freedom principles, assess conditions worldwide, defend media independence and honor journalists killed in the course of their work.

facts.label: Regional protection in Europe
facts.value: For states covered by the European Convention on Human Rights, Article 10 protects freedom of expression and the press. The Council of Europe says restrictions must be lawful and pursue a legitimate aim; European human-rights case law applies close scrutiny to such limits.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows particular reported developments involving journalists and independent media, including those in Egypt and Russia; it does not attempt to catalog every press-freedom case, law, court ruling or country condition worldwide.
